name: INA260 current, voltage & power sensor
description: Texas Instruments 16-bit current, bus-voltage and power monitor with a built-in 2 mΩ shunt: measures up to ±15 A (1.25 mA steps) on a 0–36 V bus (1.25 mV steps) over I2C. Runs on 2.7–5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit INA260 High or Low Side Voltage, Current, Power Sensor (#4226), 8-pin header VCC, GND, SCL, SDA, Alert, VBus, Vin+, Vin- plus a 2-pin screw terminal for Vin+/Vin-, I2C address 0x40 (0x41/0x44/0x45 with the A0/A1 jumpers).
eli5: Sits in the wire to a motor, LED strip or battery and tells your board how many amps are flowing, at what voltage, and how much power that is.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Logic supply 2.7–5.5 V; use the same voltage as your microcontroller (3.3 V on ESP32/Pico)

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (common with the measured circuit's ground)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up on the board)

pins.name: Alert
pins.description: Alert/conversion-ready output (open-drain, pulled up to VCC on the board); not needed for basic use

pins.name: VBus
pins.description: Bus-voltage sense input, 0–36 V; tied to Vin+ by the VB jumper (cut it for low-side sensing)

pins.name: Vin+
pins.description: Current input: from the supply (high side), max 36 V, ±15 A; same net as the screw terminal's Vin+

pins.name: Vin-
pins.description: Current output: to the load (high side); same net as the screw terminal's Vin-

supplierQuery: Adafruit INA260 current voltage power sensor breakout 4226
buildNotes: Put the INA260 in series with the load: supply + to Vin+, Vin- to the load's +. The board's GND must be joined to the measured circuit's ground.
The measured circuit may be 0–36 V and up to ±15 A, independent of VCC; carry high current through the screw terminal with thick wire, never through breadboard rows or the header pins.
Registers are 16-bit, MSB first. Current (0x01) is two's complement × 1.25 mA; bus voltage (0x02) × 1.25 mV; power (0x03) × 10 mW. Manufacturer ID (0xFE) reads 0x5449.
Default address 0x40; bridge A0 for 0x41, A1 for 0x44, both for 0x45.
For low-side sensing cut the VB jumper and wire VBus to the supply rail, otherwise the voltage and power readings are wrong.

driver.code:
# INA260 precision current, voltage & power monitor (Texas Instruments), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the TI datasheet (SBOS656C): 16-bit registers sent MSB first, fixed LSBs:
# current 1.25 mA (two's complement), bus voltage 1.25 mV, power 10 mW.
import time

_REG_CONFIG = 0x00
_REG_CURRENT = 0x01
_REG_BUS_VOLTAGE = 0x02
_REG_POWER = 0x03
_REG_MASK_ENABLE = 0x06
_REG_ALERT_LIMIT = 0x07
_REG_MANUFACTURER_ID = 0xFE
_REG_DIE_ID = 0xFF

_MANUFACTURER_ID = 0x5449  # "TI"


class INA260:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x40):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if self._read(_REG_MANUFACTURER_ID) != _MANUFACTURER_ID:
            raise OSError('INA260 not found at 0x%02X: check wiring and the A0/A1 address jumpers' % addr)

    def _read(self, reg):
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, 2)
        return (d[0] << 8) | d[1]

    def _write(self, reg, value):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([(value >> 8) & 0xFF, value & 0xFF]))

    def reset(self):
        """Reset all registers to their power-on values (config bit 15)."""
        self._write(_REG_CONFIG, 0x8000)
        time.sleep_ms(2)

    def configure(self, avg=0, vbus_ct=4, ishunt_ct=4, mode=7):
        """avg 0-7 (1,4,16,64,128,256,512,1024 samples), conversion-time codes 0-7
        (140 us ... 8.244 ms, 4 = 1.1 ms), mode 7 = continuous current and voltage (power-on default)."""
        self._write(_REG_CONFIG, 0x6000 | ((avg & 7) << 9) | ((vbus_ct & 7) << 6) | ((ishunt_ct & 7) << 3) | (mode & 7))

    def current(self):
        """Current through the integrated 2 mOhm shunt in mA (positive = Vin+ to Vin-)."""
        raw = self._read(_REG_CURRENT)
        if raw & 0x8000:
            raw -= 0x10000
        return raw * 1.25

    def voltage(self):
        """Bus voltage on VBus in volts (0-36 V)."""
        return (self._read(_REG_BUS_VOLTAGE) & 0x7FFF) * 0.00125

    def power(self):
        """Power in mW as computed by the chip (|current| x bus voltage)."""
        return self._read(_REG_POWER) * 10

    def conversion_ready(self):
        """True once a new conversion is complete (reading clears the flag)."""
        return bool(self._read(_REG_MASK_ENABLE) & 0x0008)

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from ina260 import INA260

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = INA260(i2c)
while True:
    print('V=%.3fV I=%.1fmA' % (sensor.voltage(), sensor.current()))
    time.sleep(1)
